sections.title: Ultimatum, transit and provisioning
sections.text: The Romanian ultimatum, Hungarian movement instructions and Arad provisioning request document the deadlines, permissions and supplies governing withdrawal. The Arad request specifies 80,000 men and 30,000 animals.
cases: The Romanian ultimatum in the evening report

sections.title: Transport and medical provision
sections.text: Transit planning, provisions requests and recommendations for heated sick wagons record preparations for moving personnel. The medical instructions specify stoves, cooking equipment and hot tea for return transports from Turkey.
cases: Heated sick wagons and medical return transport

sections.title: Command, internment and unrest
sections.text: Mackensen’s appeal and the internment correspondence concern the conditions under which his forces could return. The separate Kiev reports describe unrest and the soldiers’ council’s stated neutrality.
cases: Kiev unrest and soldiers’ council neutrality

sections.title: Cargo, loading and release
sections.text: Reports from Nikolaev and Poti concern cargo on hand, loading opportunities and the release of supplies. Tobacco ready for loading and an inquiry about oil establish availability or a requested decision, without establishing that either consignment departed.
cases: Nikolaev supply cargo and shipping decisions

sections.title: Ship sales, payment and authority
sections.text: The proposed Corcovado terms allocate seizure and nonpayment risks. Other Turkish purchase proposals require immediate payment and authorization; naval armistice instructions provide a separate record of command requirements.

sections.title: Cash supply and denominations
sections.text: The crown requests specify wages and purchases in Hungary, delivery by aircraft and a suitable supply of small notes. A complete parallel reception restores the ending of the daily airlift instruction.
cases: Thirty million crowns requested for wages and purchases
One million crowns daily by ordinary aircraft

sections.title: Remittance, payout and guarded transport
sections.text: The Vienna–Kronstadt bank-transfer message asks whether local payment succeeded. Later correspondence concerns a guarded rail alternative, access to an advance at Arad and continuing banknote shortages.
cases: An initial five-million-crown transfer through Vienna
A guarded rail alternative for Hermannstadt cash
Arad advances and partial crown remittances

sections.title: Procurement cancellation and resale
sections.text: ZITAG orders distinguish further commitments from consignments already paid for. Silk purchases are to be resold where removal is uncertain; a separate Odessa instruction seeks a wagon sale on the best possible terms.
cases: Purchase stop-orders and the paid-consignment exception
Local resale of silk when transport is uncertain

sections.title: Allowances and currency redemption
sections.text: Allowance instructions and exchange correspondence concern the terms on which money could be paid or redeemed. The lei negotiations distinguish stamped from unstamped notes, while several numerical rate fields remain unresolved.
cases: Negotiations over stamped and unstamped lei notes

sections.title: Schedules, retransmission and wire connections
sections.text: Eilvese listening periods, repeated telegrams and the Odessa wire-connection report document the operation of the communications network. Parallel receptions preserve wording lost or damaged in individual copies.

sections.title: Cipher instructions and service procedure
sections.text: The Tiflis instruction and Ringbahn key-reuse messages concern continued communication under specified cipher arrangements. September procedure messages provide an earlier record of radio-service practice.

sections.title: Vehicles, equipment and departures
sections.text: Vehicle and trailer requests, readiness orders and a reported truck departure accompany the Seifert station and personnel traffic. Postponements, arrival enquiries and meal preparations document distinct stages of departure. The [transport and demobilisation study](../../docs/historical-studies/transport-and-demobilisation.md) compares these records and their unresolved places and timings.
cases: Trucks, trailers, readiness and the Hanau destination
Station control and Seifert’s arrival and departure messages
November 12 arrival, departure and car enquiries
Postponed departure, supper enquiry and farewell

sections.title: Civilian residence, travel and discharge
sections.text: The Constantinople civilian instructions, Kremp’s departure enquiry and Rudolf’s discharge request concern permission to remain, arrangements to travel and release from service. Each records a different administrative decision or request.
cases: Kremp’s request for a departure date

sections.title: Transfers, recalls and return to units
sections.text: Staff transfers and military-mission recalls continued during withdrawal. These messages identify offices, destinations and service relationships; the medical return instruction concerns rejoining a unit.

sections.title: Mission staffing, equipment and procurement
sections.text: October correspondence with the Caucasus concerns personnel, equipment, supplies and routing around Tiflis. These records describe the mission’s administrative work before the later withdrawal instructions.

sections.title: Representation, Poti traffic and withdrawal
sections.text: The Tiflis appointment concerns Polish representation. Separate Poti and armistice messages document transport-related communication and withdrawal instructions; their source editions retain damaged passages and differences between receptions.
cases: The damaged first part of the Poti message
A withdrawal notice preserved in two receptions
